Hello everyone, I'm Thor from Denmark in the north of Europe. I'm here to tell you a little bit about OUAS ;)

This is day 1,099 and we have reached 116 countries across 4 continents!

You are welcome to Ask Me Anything, read up on it here below or watch this short video to get some quick answers: https://youtu.be/igfIQ8STDco

Welcome one and all! :)

What is OUAS?

Once Upon A Saga is a complicated logistical challenge of historical proportions! It also has great humanitarian value and a source for inspiration for many who cross its path.

In short, the "Saga" is the quest for 1 man to reach every single country in the World in a single unbroken journey - completely without the use of flight! Although the World has been conquered geographically by travellers many times throughout history, a flightless journey is a feat that has never before been achieved...until now.

In order to understand the "Saga" better it can be seen as 3 individual projects:

1) A journey to every country without flight with all of its complicated logistics (203 countries).

2) A positive promotion of each country sharing stories of positive experiences to counter the negatives often seen in the media.

3) A positive promotion of the Red Cross Red Crescent movement, which was founded in 1863 and today spans across 190 nations.

As such, the Saga is known to provide three elements for those who partake: - Inspiration - Entertainment - Education

So, join us on the journey by spreading the word, that A STRANGER IS A FRIEND YOU'VE NEVER MET BEFORE! ;)

I was, like you, very high strung, and I let pretty much everything get me going, either anxiety, rage, or a combination of both.

For some reason, I ended up picking up a book by Epictetus, a Roman slave who followed the Stoic philosophy, at some college library book sale.

In it, he wrote about "Externals" and "Internals." Internals are things you control. They are YOUR actions, YOUR feelings. Externals are things that happen to you, things you really can't control. Fired form your job, that annoying guy keeps talking to you, that person who gossips and lies about you behind your back, or even that complete idiot in the Blue Civic who drives like crap in front of you.

I found that I was constantly worrying about all these external things, like struggling to pay the bills, what so and so said about me, my car breaking down AGAIN, getting that promotion, trying to do 'X' because my parents wanted me to, etc. to the point where I couldn't focus on anything else. And the INTERNAL ME pretty much disappeared.

Once I had read that passage, I realized, I'm super unhappy all the time. I'm not any fun to be around, I hate life, this SUCKS. And it was all because I let these External things eat up my time and effort. I can't please everybody, and I was getting nowhere because of it. So, I started thinking. What am I doing to myself? Can I control the fact that I don;t have enough money to pay the bills? Well, YES I DO! Spend less! Make More! Instead of worrying about that promotion to get that raise, which are External things, I started doing things that I controlled. Like skipping out on Thursday night happy hour that cost me $30 a week. There's the insurance bill for the month. I also worked a second job a couple days a week instead, making fuckall in $$, but it was still a positive value instead of spending. It made up about another $200/month, which I used to pay off that damn credit card bill that kept calling me. In a year, it was gone, and I realized that using Internal efforts, I removed an External pressure.

I did they same with the gossipy type of people. Instead of reacting to it (usually terribly, by instigating screaming matches or acting out in other immature ways), I realized that I couldn't control their words, but I COULD control how I reacted to it. I focused on my reactions to their lies, and did nothing. I didn't fight back, I didn't get upset (this took a while - I focused on not being Outwardly upset), and as I calmed my own reaction, people began taking my side. Why? Because all those lies the other person told about me just made THEM look bad and the fool. But people couldn't see that because of my (over) reaction to it previously. Only by controlling the Internal response was I able to overcome another External. To this day, I still do not talk bad about people. I simply don't do it. And in the end, it was my reactions that were delaying my work promotion. people saw me act out, and determined (rightly, I suppose!) that I was not ready. Only as I changed my actions did that which I had worked for come to me. In essence, I was the person blocking my promotion, simply by worrying so much about it.

In the end, I realized that the only thing that matters to myself, and to those around me (for the most part), was my internals - what I say, what I do. People see those things that bother you, and if you react poorly, they react to your reaction, not to the initial thing that set you off. Let me say that again - THEY REACT TO YOUR REACTION. By calming myself, and not letting these External things bother me, I made myself a better person, not only for myself, but for everyone around me, as well.

My advice?

Think about and write down all the things you are worried or anxious about.
Start marking them External or Internal by asking Can you control it? If yes, it's an Internal. If no, It's an external. If it's an Internal, what are YOU going to do about changing that? Or do you even need to?

For the Externals, can you DO anything to alleviate or mitigate the external's EFFECT on you? If yes, than work on those things that you can do. make a new "Mitigation list" of the things you can do to remove an External effect. (Like my "can't pay the bills" issue above.) If no, then there is nothing to worry about. It will happen to you, or it will not. You can't affect the outcome, so let it happen naturally. (Like my gossiper issue above. I cannot control the gossiper, so I stopped reacting to it or spending any energy on it. And it naturally went its course.)
